table.name: TLGNC_CRONSTATUS
table.description: Stores status information about various time-controlled background jobs.

column.name: CRONSTATUS_NAME
column.description: Name of the cron job (unique). The same key is used as in application.xml.

column.name: LAST_START_TS
column.description: Set (and committed) by the job executor immediately when the job starts.

column.name: LAST_END_TS
column.description: Set (and committed) by the job executor when it finishes. The job executor must set this date even when the background job does nothing, or fails with an error. If start_ts > end_ts, a process is running (to make this visible to an admin, to allow a controlled shutdown with no running background jobs).

column.name: LAST_RUN_NUMBER
column.description: Used to mark log messages or imported records as belonging together: mark not just as a flag or timestamp, but possibly set records to the run_number, when it was processed (or attempted to process). Usage is optional by the job. If a background job is using this run_number, it must increment and commit it when it's started.

column.name: NEW_DATA_AVAILABLE_TS
column.description: Optional timestamp used to communicate with background job. Meaning is: if > last_end_ts, there is data to be processed. If < last_end_ts, nothing has changed and the background job can skip (without even setting last_start_ts, last_run_number). If null: not used to communicate with job; job will find out directly with a quick query if there are things to be done.
